comparisons.peer_topic: Discrete desktop and notebook GPU products
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's Radeon discrete GPUs for desktop and notebook PCs support modern APIs like DirectX 12 Ultimate and Vulkan, offer high-refresh rate displays, and leverage the RDNA 3 architecture for high performance in gaming and AI/ML computing, all supported by the regularly updated Adrenalin Edition software.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures describe hardware products designed for high-performance computing and AI workloads, but they target different segments of the stack. MU focuses on HBM memory components that enhance bandwidth and power efficiency for AI ecosystem qualifications, specifically noting the volume production of 8-high 24GB HBM3E. In contrast, AMD describes its Radeon discrete GPUs which leverage RDNA 3 architecture to deliver high performance for gaming and AI/ML computing, supported by specific software tools. While both address AI acceleration, MU's disclosure is centered on memory capacity and efficiency advancements, whereas AMD's is focused on graphics processing architecture and software ecosystems for end-user devices.

sentences.text: In 2024, we began volume production of our 8-high 24GB HBM3E with increased bandwidth and superior power efficiency enabled by our advanced 1β process node.
We have also started shipments of production-capable HBM3E 12-high 36GB units to enable qualifications across the AI ecosystem.

Our AMD Radeon discrete GPU processors for desktop and notebook PCs support current generation application programming interfaces (APIs) like DirectX® 12 Ultimate and Vulkan®, support high-refresh rate displays and include the latest technologies for immersive gaming experiences and high-performance AI/ML computing.
Our current Radeon RX 7000 Series graphics, based on the AMD RDNA™ 3 architecture, deliver high performance for the latest gaming and creation workloads.

comparisons.peer_topic: 2024 Process Node Manufacturing Status and Roadmap Changes
comparisons.peer_summary: As of the end of 2024, most products were manufactured using the Intel 7 node, while high-volume production of the Intel 4 and Intel 3 nodes was shifted to Ireland. The company canceled the productization of Intel 20A to focus on the improved Intel 18A node, which is expected to enter high-volume production in 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures reflect the semiconductor industry's intense focus on process technology and manufacturing status, but they detail different nodes and strategic decisions. MU highlights the successful volume production of HBM3E using its advanced 1β process node, emphasizing performance metrics like bandwidth and thermal response for AI applications. INTC describes the operational status of its own process nodes (Intel 7, 4, and 3), noting the shift of EUV lithography nodes (Intel 4 and 3) to Ireland and the cancellation of Intel 20A to focus on Intel 18A. While MU's disclosure signals readiness and competitive capability in advanced memory processes for AI, INTC's disclosure outlines internal manufacturing shifts and roadmap pivots in its CPU-focused node strategy.

sentences.text: In 2024, we began volume production of our 8-high 24GB HBM3E with increased bandwidth and superior power efficiency enabled by our advanced 1β process node.

This enhanced version of the third generation of HBM delivers faster data rates, improved thermal response, and a higher monolithic die density within the same package footprint as previous generations.

As of the end of 2024, a significant majority of our products were manufactured using our Intel 7 process node in Arizona and Israel, we successfully ramped our Intel 4 and Intel 3 process nodes as our first EUV lithography nodes and shifted high-volume production of those nodes to Ireland, and we canceled the productization of our Intel 20A process node to focus efforts on the improved version of the node, Intel 18A, that we expect to put into high-volume production in 2025 with our new client family of products code-named Panther Lake.

comparisons.peer_topic: RTX AI ecosystem and market position
comparisons.peer_summary: RTX GPUs accelerate AI applications, and with an installed base of over 100 million AI-capable PCs and 500+ RTX AI-enabled applications, RTX is the AI PC leader.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures identify AI as a key driver for their respective product lines, yet they operate at different layers of the computing stack. MU reports advancing HBM3E memory technology with increased bandwidth and power efficiency to support AI ecosystem qualifications. NVDA highlights its RTX GPUs as leaders in the AI PC market, accelerating AI applications on a large installed base of over 100 million AI-capable PCs. MU's advancement is in high-bandwidth memory infrastructure, while NVDA's is in the GPU compute platforms that utilize such memory, both contributing to the broader AI hardware ecosystem but addressing distinct product categories (memory vs. GPU).

comparisons.peer_topic: AI research focus and on-device capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The company conducts broad research and development across AI, including generative AI, with the goal of advancing core capabilities to run on-device and scaling them across industries, leveraging over a decade of investments focused on power efficiency and personalization.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies emphasize AI as a critical area of research and development, but with different technical focuses and deployment goals. MU details the physical manufacturing and specification advancements of HBM3E memory (e.g., 1β process node, power efficiency) to enable AI workloads. QCOM describes its broad R&D efforts in generative AI with a specific strategic goal of advancing core AI capabilities to run on-device for consumer experiences, leveraging investments in power efficiency and personalization. While MU's disclosure is product-centric regarding memory hardware specifications for AI servers/systems, QCOM's is strategy-centric regarding on-device AI processing for mobile/connected devices.
